title: 4.3 Load test
CI should build images independently of test results for non-main branches
description:
## Problem
Currently the CI workflow (service-ci.yml) has this dependency chain:
1. All service test jobs must complete
2. Lint job runs (depends on all test jobs)
3. Build-images job runs (depends on lint)

If ANY test fails, images are never built. This blocks:
- Development iteration (dev images)
- Staging deployment (staging images)

## Current State (service-ci.yml)

```yaml
lint:
  needs:
    - admin-api-service
    - ai-aas-cli
    - analytics-service
    - api-router-service
    - hello-service
    - user-org-service
    - world-service

build-images:
  needs: [lint]
```

## Proposed Solution
For develop and staging branches:
- Build images in parallel with tests (remove needs dependency)
- Use conditional logic to only block main branch builds on test/lint results
- Add warning annotation to images built with failing tests

## Implementation

1. Modify `build-images` job:
```yaml
build-images:
  name: Build and Push Images
  needs: []  # No longer depend on lint/tests
  if: github.event_name == 'push'
  ...
```

2. Add a separate "gate" job for main branch that requires all checks:
```yaml
production-gate:
  name: Production Gate
  needs: [lint, build-images]
  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
  ...
```

## Files to Modify

- `.github/workflows/service-ci.yml`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] develop branch: Images build even if tests fail
- [ ] staging branch: Images build even if tests fail
- [ ] main branch: Images only build if all tests pass
- [ ] Failed test builds have warning labels in container registry
- [ ] CI runtime reduced for develop/staging branches

## Benefits
- Faster development iteration
- Staging can test latest code even if some tests are temporarily broken
- Production (main) still requires passing tests

title: Fix API Router to use revision-independent KServe service endpoints

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Issue Description

The API Router backend endpoints in `values-development.yaml` are hardcoded to specific KServe revision numbers (e.g., `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private`). This causes the API Router to break when KServe garbage collects old revisions.

## Current State

`services/api-router-service/deployments/helm/api-router-service/values-development.yaml`:
```yaml
backends:
  endpoints: "unsloth/gpt-oss-20b:http://unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private.development.svc.cluster.local:8012,..."
```

## Problems

1. **Brittle**: When KServe rolls out revision 00002, 00001 still exists but will eventually be garbage collected
2. **Manual updates required**: Every InferenceService update requires manual Helm values change
3. **Non-existent backend**: Configuration includes `openai/gpt-oss-20b` which doesn't exist
4. **Inconsistent state**: InferenceService is on revision 00002, but API Router points to 00001

## Root Cause

KServe revisions change on every InferenceService spec update. Hardcoding revision numbers violates the principle of declarative, self-healing infrastructure.

## Solution Options

1. **Use revision-independent service**: `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b.development.svc.cluster.local`
   - Pros: Automatic routing to active revision
   - Cons: Comment in Helm values says port 80 causes Istio timeouts
   - Need to test if this still applies

2. **Dynamic discovery**: API Router queries KServe API for active revisions
   - Pros: Always uses correct revision
   - Cons: Requires KServe API client, more complexity

3. **Automation**: CI/CD script updates Helm values on InferenceService changes
   - Pros: Keeps using -private services on port 8012
   - Cons: Adds CI/CD complexity, still manual intervention

## Recommended Approach

Test option 1 (revision-independent service) first. The timeout issue may have been fixed or may not apply to the -private service variant. If successful, update all backend endpoints to use revision-independent services.

## Files to Update

- `services/api-router-service/deployments/helm/api-router-service/values-development.yaml`
- Consider: `values-staging.yaml`, `values-production.yaml` if they exist

## Acceptance Criteria

- API Router uses revision-independent service endpoints
- Inference requests continue to work after KServe revision changes
- Remove non-existent `openai/gpt-oss-20b` backend entry
- Document the endpoint pattern in Helm chart comments

## Root Cause Analysis

**Category**: missing_context / config_drift

**Flow Analysis**:
1. Pod has OPENAI_API_KEY env var from secret -> CORRECT
2. guidellm-runner process has access to this env var -> CORRECT

- Runner code expects api_key in YAML config (Application layer)
- No bridge between them

comments.text:
# Investigation Report

**Bead**: ai-aas-0to4
**Date**: 2025-12-14
**Investigator**: debugger agent

## Symptom

GuideLLM runner pod in monitoring namespace fails to run benchmarks. All requests return 401 Unauthorized. Benchmark results show zero requests completed.

## Reproduction

1. Pod runs successfully, logs show "starting benchmark loop"
2. After ~15 seconds, logs show "benchmark completed with ZERO requests"
3. API Router logs show multiple 401 responses with "missing X-API-Key header"
4. Pattern repeats every 5 minutes (300s interval)

## Evidence Gathered

| Source | Finding |
|--------|---------|
| runner.go:112-115 | Only passes API key to subprocess if target.APIKey \!= "" |
| config.go:28 | Target.APIKey populated from YAML only (yaml:"api_key,omitempty") |
| ConfigMap | No api_key fields in target configs |
| Deployment | OPENAI_API_KEY env var correctly set from secret |
| Pod env | Confirmed: OPENAI_API_KEY=ai-aas_gX0-... exists |
| API Router logs | All requests: "missing X-API-Key header", 401 status |

## Hypotheses Tested

| Hypothesis | Verdict | Evidence |
|------------|---------|----------|
| URL doubled path issue | ✅ FIXED | Prior work fixed this |
| API endpoint broken | ❌ Ruled out | Manual curl with auth works |
| Env var not set in pod | ❌ Ruled out | kubectl exec confirms it exists |
| API key not passed to subprocess | ✅ CONFIRMED | Code path skipped due to empty target.APIKey |

## Root Cause

**Category**: config_drift

**Explanation**: The guidellm-runner has two disconnected configuration systems:

1. **Kubernetes layer**: Sets OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable from secret (working correctly)
2. **Application layer**: Expects api_key in YAML config file (target.api_key field)

The runner code (runner.go:113) only passes the API key to the guidellm subprocess if target.APIKey is populated from YAML. However, the ConfigMap config does not include api_key fields, so this condition is never true.

The OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable exists in the pod but is never read by the runner code.

**Evidence**: Lines 112-115 in runner.go show conditional logic that is never executed.

## Context Gap Check

- [X] Was this caused by missing context? NO

This is a deployment/configuration issue, not a missing development pattern or rule.

## Proposed Fix

**High-level description**: Bridge the gap between environment variable and application config.

**Option 1 (Recommended)**: Modify runner code to fall back to environment variable
- In runner.go:112-115, if target.APIKey is empty, read from os.Getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
- Maintains backward compatibility with YAML-based config
- Follows 12-factor app principles (config from environment)

**Option 2**: Populate api_key in YAML from Helm values
- Modify Helm chart to template api_key fields in config.yaml
- Requires passing secret value through Helm values (not ideal)
- Creates duplication between secret and ConfigMap

**Affected files**:
- /home/dev/guidellm-runner/internal/runner/runner.go - needs fallback logic

**Estimated complexity**: Low (5-10 lines of code)

## Prevention

How to prevent this class of bug in future:

| Type | Action |
|------|--------|
| Test | Add integration test that verifies API key is passed to subprocess |
| Test | Add test that validates env var fallback logic |
| Logging | Add debug log showing which API key source was used |
| Documentation | Document environment variable fallback behavior |

Will create in next step.

title: Worker: Implement background job worker
description:
# Background Job Worker Implementation

## Overview
Implement a worker that polls the database for pending pull jobs and executes them.

## Location
`services/admin-api-service/internal/worker/`

## Components

### worker.go - Main Worker Loop
```go
type Worker struct {
    db         *pgxpool.Pool
    pullSvc    *pull.Service  // From shared library
    interval   time.Duration
    shutdownCh chan struct{}
}

func (w *Worker) Run(ctx context.Context) error
func (w *Worker) Stop()
```

### job.go - Job Execution
- Claim job atomically (UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending' RETURNING)
- Execute pull using shared library
- Update progress periodically
- Handle completion/failure
- Check for cancellation

## Key Features
1. **Atomic job claiming**: Prevent race conditions with multiple workers
2. **Progress updates**: Update bytes_downloaded periodically (every 10s or 10MB)
3. **Cancellation checking**: Check job status before each file download
4. **Graceful shutdown**: Finish current job on SIGTERM, don't pick up new ones
5. **Error handling**: Retry transient errors, fail permanently on others
6. **Credential access**: Retrieve HF token and S3 creds from platform_credentials table

## Configuration
```yaml
worker:
  enabled: true
  poll_interval: 5s
  max_concurrent_jobs: 1  # Start with 1, scale later
  progress_update_interval: 10s
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Worker starts with admin-api-service when enabled
- [ ] Jobs are claimed atomically (no duplicates)
- [ ] Progress is updated during download
- [ ] Cancellation stops download promptly
- [ ] Graceful shutdown works correctly
- [ ] Comprehensive unit tests

title: Server-side model caching (background job worker)
Clean up stale Knative revisions holding GPU resources
description:
## Problem

When InferenceServices are updated, old Knative revisions may continue running and hold GPU resources, even when they're not receiving traffic.

### Observed Behavior

`mistral-7b-instruct-development` had 3 revisions running (00001, 00002, 00003), each holding a GPU:
- 00001: Running but stale
- 00002: Latest ready (active traffic)
- 00003: CrashLoopBackOff but still allocating GPU

This consumed 3 GPUs when only 1 was needed.

## Solution

Options:
1. **Configure revision retention**: Set `revisionHistoryLimit` on InferenceService to automatically clean up old revisions
2. **Create operator logic**: Add cleanup logic in ai-model-operator to delete stale revisions
3. **Configure Knative**: Set cluster-wide defaults for revision garbage collection

## Files

- KServe/Knative configuration or ai-model-operator reconciliation logic

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Completion Summary

**Status**: ✅ Complete

**What was done**:
- Created `/infra/k8s/knative-serving/config-gc.yaml` with aggressive GC settings for GPU workloads
- Configured `min-non-active-revisions: 1` to keep only 1 old revision for rollback
- Configured `max-non-active-revisions: 2` to prevent GPU resource buildup
- Set `retain-since-last-active-time: 5m` for quick cleanup of inactive revisions
- Set `retain-since-create-time: 10m` to clean up failed/CrashLoopBackOff revisions
- Added documentation in operator README explaining revision GC configuration
- Added code comment in InferenceService builder referencing the GC config

**Files changed**:
- `infra/k8s/knative-serving/config-gc.yaml` - New ConfigMap with GPU-optimized GC settings
- `operators/ai-model-operator/README.md` - Added "Revision Garbage Collection" section
- `operators/ai-model-operator/internal/kserve/inferenceservice.go` - Added GC documentation comment

**CRD changes**:
- None (cluster-wide Knative configuration only)

**Tests added/updated**:
- No tests needed (configuration-only change)

**Documentation updated**:
- `operators/ai-model-operator/README.md` - Documented GC settings and rationale

**Related beads created**:
- None (deployment will be handled through existing GitOps workflow)

**Commit**: e64a4448 (combined with retry logic improvements)

**How it works**:
The config-gc ConfigMap is managed by ArgoCD via the knative-config Application. When synced to the cluster, Knative's garbage collector will automatically clean up old revisions based on these rules:
1. Active revisions (receiving traffic) are never deleted
2. Keep minimum 1 non-active revision for quick rollback
3. Delete non-active revisions after 5 minutes of inactivity
4. Delete failed/unused revisions after 10 minutes of creation
5. Never keep more than 2 non-active revisions total

This prevents the issue where mistral-7b-instruct had 3 revisions (00001, 00002, 00003) each holding a GPU, wasting 2 GPUs on stale revisions.

title: Document anti-pattern: Runtime network dependencies in Go services
close_reason: IMPLEMENTED: commit edc15689 - Added anti-pattern for runtime network dependencies to context/agents.md and context/go-services-developer/agents.md

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Context

Investigation ai-aas-y1y9 identified a missing anti-pattern in the codebase context documentation.

## Problem

The tiktoken-go library downloads BPE vocabulary files from the internet at runtime. This caused API Router to fail in Kubernetes where outbound internet is blocked. The pattern should have been documented to prevent similar issues.

## Task

Add to `context/go-services-developer/agents.md` (or create new file):

### Section: Runtime Data Dependencies

**Anti-pattern: Libraries that download data at runtime**
```
❌ WRONG: Use tiktoken-go without offline mode
import "github.com/pkoukk/tiktoken-go"
// Downloads BPE files from internet on first use
encoding, err := tiktoken.GetEncoding("cl100k_base")

✅ CORRECT: Use tiktoken-go-loader with embedded data
import "github.com/pkoukk/tiktoken-go-loader"
// BPE files embedded in binary
encoding, err := tiktoken_loader.GetEncoding("cl100k_base")

✅ ALTERNATIVE: Pre-download and cache in Docker image
RUN mkdir -p /app/tiktoken-cache && \
    go run scripts/download-tiktoken-data.go /app/tiktoken-cache
ENV TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR=/app/tiktoken-cache
```

**Principle**: All runtime data must be embedded in the binary or container image. Never download data from the internet at runtime in production services.

**Known problematic libraries**:
- tiktoken-go (use tiktoken-go-loader instead)
- (add others as discovered)

## Related

- ai-aas-y1y9 (investigation)
- ai-aas-k0p2 (fix)

title: CLI org command ignores --profile endpoint settings

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Bug Description

The `ai-aas-cli org create` (and other org/user/apikey commands) ignores the `--profile` flag for endpoint resolution.

**Root Cause:**
In `internal/admin/org.go` line 310, the command uses `config.Load()` instead of `config.GetEffectiveConfig(profileName)`:

```go
// Current (WRONG)
cfg, err := config.Load()

// Should be
cfg, _, err := config.GetEffectiveConfig(flagProfile)
```

**Expected Behavior:**
When running `ai-aas-cli org create --profile staging-sg`, the command should use the endpoints defined in the `staging-sg` profile.

**Actual Behavior:**
The `--profile` flag is only used to *save* the org_id after creation, not to *load* the profile's endpoint settings.

**Error:**
```
$ ai-aas-cli org create --name stg-org --slug stg-org --profile staging-sg
Error: Service 'user-org-service' is unavailable: Endpoint: https://user-org.dev.ai-aas.local
# Should use https://user-org.staging.otherjamesbrown.com from staging-sg profile
```

**Workaround:**
Use explicit flags:
```bash
ai-aas-cli org create --name stg-org --slug stg-org \
  --user-org-endpoint https://user-org.staging.otherjamesbrown.com \
  --api-key <staging-api-key>
```

**Files to Fix:**
- `services/ai-aas-cli/internal/admin/org.go`
- `services/ai-aas-cli/internal/admin/user.go`
- `services/ai-aas-cli/internal/admin/apikey.go`

All commands in internal/admin/ that call `config.Load()` should be updated to use `config.GetEffectiveConfig()`.

title: Add --model-access flag to CLI user create command
description:
## Problem
CLI user creation doesn't allow specifying model access mode. Admins need to:
1. Create user
2. Separately call `user model-access set-mode`

This should be a single step.

## Proposed Solution
Add `--model-access` flag to `ai-aas-cli user create`:
```bash
ai-aas-cli user create --org-id myorg --email user@test.com --model-access all
ai-aas-cli user create --org-id myorg --email user@test.com --model-access restricted
```

## Files to Modify
- `services/ai-aas-cli/internal/admin/user.go`
  - Add `--model-access` flag to create command
  - Values: `all` (maps to auto_grant), `restricted`
  - Default: `restricted` for non-admin, `all` for admin role

## Implementation
1. Add flag to `userCreateCommand()`:
```go
cmd.Flags().StringVar(&flagModelAccess, "model-access", "", "Model access mode: 'all' or 'restricted' (default: auto for admin role)")
```

2. After user creation, if flag is set:
```go
if flagModelAccess != "" {
    accessMode := "restricted"
    if flagModelAccess == "all" {
        accessMode = "auto_grant"
    }
    // Call user-org-service to set access mode
    err := client.SetUserAccessMode(ctx, orgID, userID, accessMode)
    if err != nil {
        // Warn but don't fail
    }
}
```

## User-Org Service API
May need to add/verify endpoint exists:
```
PUT /v1/orgs/{orgId}/users/{userId}/model-access
{"access_mode": "auto_grant"}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--model-access all` sets auto_grant mode
- [ ] `--model-access restricted` sets restricted mode
- [ ] Default behavior: admin role → all, non-admin → restricted
- [ ] Help text documents the flag
- [ ] Works with `--format json` output

## Testing
```bash
# Create with explicit all access
ai-aas-cli user create --org-id myorg --email power@test.com --model-access all
ai-aas-cli user model-access show --org-id myorg --email power@test.com
# Expected: auto_grant

# Create with explicit restricted access
ai-aas-cli user create --org-id myorg --email basic@test.com --model-access restricted
ai-aas-cli user model-access show --org-id myorg --email basic@test.com
# Expected: restricted
```

title: Model deployment should auto-create global routing policy
description:
## Problem
When deploying a model via `ai-aas-cli model deploy create`, no routing policy is automatically created. This causes inference requests to fail with:
```
Error: Operation failed: failed to send request: chat completion failed: status 500, body: {"error":"no routing policy configured","code":"ROUTING_ERROR"}
```

## Root Causes Found

### 1. Missing Auto-Create Implementation (Fixed - code ready)
The `ModelRegistration` domain has `AutoCreatePolicy` field but it was never implemented.

**Fix Applied:**
- Modified `services/admin-api-service/internal/service/registry.go` to auto-create a global routing policy when a new model is registered
- Updated `internal/api/router.go` to inject the PolicyRepository into ModelRegistryService

### 2. Missing Database Table (Fixed - applied)
The `routing_policies` table did not exist in the database.

**Fix Applied:**
- Applied migration `20251126001_routing_policies.up.sql` via k8s Job

### 3. Architecture Gap: Policy Sync (Fixed - code ready)
**Critical Discovery:** The Admin API Service stores policies in PostgreSQL, but the API Router Service reads them from etcd/BoltDB cache. There was **no sync mechanism**.

**Fix Applied:**
- Created `services/api-router-service/internal/config/admin_sync.go` - Sync client that fetches policies from Admin API
- Updated `services/api-router-service/internal/config/config.go` - Added config fields
- Updated `services/api-router-service/cmd/router/main.go` - Integration
- Updated Helm deployment and values files

### 4. Manual Routing Policies Created (applied)
- gpt-oss-20b → unsloth/gpt-oss-20b:100%
- mistral-7b → mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3:100%

### 5. Secret Created (applied)

title: Optimize operator-developer/agents.md
Investigate: KServe not cleaning up old pods after memory limit change

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Prior Investigation (from issue ai-aas-53sw)

**Symptom**: When memory limits were changed from 32Gi → 24Gi in ai-aas-config, KServe/Knative created new pods but did NOT terminate old pods with outdated configuration.

**Current State**:
| Model | Old Pod (32Gi) | Restarts | New Pod (24Gi) |
|-------|----------------|----------|----------------|
| mistral-7b | Running (00001) | 367 | Running (00130) |
| openai-gpt-oss-20b | Running (00001) | 374 | Running (00146) |
| unsloth-gpt-oss-20b | Running (00001) | 425 | NONE |

**Impact**: 
- Traffic is split between old (32Gi) and new (24Gi) pods
- Old pods continue hitting OOM because they still have higher memory limits
- Rolling update appears stuck - old revisions not being terminated

**Already Tried**:
- Modified memory limits in ai-aas-config
- GitOps push triggered ArgoCD sync
- New pods created with correct limits
- Old pods remain running

**Expected Behavior**: 
KServe should:
1. Create new Knative Revision with updated spec ✅ (working)
2. Gradually shift traffic to new revision (unknown status)
3. Scale down and delete old revision once traffic shifted ❌ (NOT happening)

**Hypotheses to Test**:
1. Knative Serving garbage collection disabled or misconfigured
2. Traffic not fully shifted to new revisions (canary/progressive rollout stuck)
3. GPU resource constraints blocking old pod termination
4. KServe/Knative operator errors during reconciliation
5. Configuration issue in InferenceService spec preventing cleanup

**Files to Examine**:
- InferenceService definitions in ai-aas-config
- Knative Serving config-gc ConfigMap
- KServe controller logs
- Knative Serving revision status and traffic routing

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Key Evidence Gathered

### 1. Revision Status
All three InferenceServices show the SAME pattern:
- **LatestCreatedRevision**: 00153/00173/00159 (new, with updated config)
- **LatestReadyRevision**: 00001 (old, original config)
- **LatestRolledoutRevision**: 00001 (old, original config)
- **Traffic**: 100% to revision 00001 (old)

### 2. New Revisions Are UNSCHEDULABLE
All new revisions are in 'Unschedulable' state with error:
```
0/8 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient cpu, 8 Insufficient memory, 8 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
```

### 3. GPU Resource Exhaustion
Cluster has 5 GPU nodes, each with 1 GPU:
- lke531921-776664-2d6917d80000: 1 GPU
- lke531921-776664-37342cf80000: 1 GPU  
- lke531921-776664-46225a090000: 1 GPU (running mistral-00001)
- lke531921-776664-51386eeb0000: 1 GPU (running openai-00001)
- lke531921-776664-59eb445b0000: 1 GPU (running unsloth-00001)

All GPUs are OCCUPIED by the old revision pods. No free GPU available for new revisions.

### 4. Traffic Routing
All traffic is routed to revision 00001:
```yaml
traffic:
  - latestRevision: true
    percent: 100
    revisionName: mistral-7b-instruct-v03-predictor-00001
```

Despite `latestRevision: true`, traffic stays on 00001 because it's the ONLY ready revision.

### 5. Knative Garbage Collection Config
```yaml
max-non-active-revisions: "2"
min-non-active-revisions: "1"
retain-since-create-time: 10m
retain-since-last-active-time: 5m
```

GC is properly configured but CANNOT act because revision 00001 is ACTIVE (serving traffic).

### 6. KServe Controller Logs
Controller repeatedly detects configuration drift (memory: 32Gi→24Gi) and creates new revisions, but they remain unschedulable. No errors in controller - it's working correctly.

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED

### The Real Problem: Conflicting ArgoCD Applications

TWO ArgoCD applications are managing the same AIModel CRs:

1. **aimodels-development** (ai-aas repo)
   - Source: `infra/k8s/aimodels/development/`
   - Contains STALE config: memory=32Gi
   - Status: OutOfSync but WINNING the conflict

2. **aimodels-config-development** (ai-aas-config repo)
   - Source: `environments/development/models/`
   - Contains NEW config: memory=24Gi (from commit febe54a)
   - Status: Synced but LOSING the conflict

### Why Old Pods Can't Be Replaced

1. User updated ai-aas-config repo (24Gi) ✅
2. ArgoCD synced aimodels-config-development ✅
3. BUT aimodels-development keeps reverting to 32Gi ❌
4. AIModel operator creates new InferenceService revisions with 32Gi
5. New pods with 32Gi try to schedule but NO GPU AVAILABLE
6. Old pods with 32Gi stay running (serving traffic)
7. Knative GC CANNOT delete old pods because they're ACTIVE
8. System stuck in rollout deadlock

### The Deadlock

```
Old Pod (32Gi) → Running on GPU1 → Serving traffic
New Pod (32Gi) → Pending (no GPU) → Cannot become ready
Traffic → 100% to old pod (only ready pod)
GC → Cannot delete old pod (it's active)
```

This is NOT a KServe/Knative bug. It's a CONFIGURATION CONFLICT causing a resource deadlock.

**Root Cause**:

The AIModel CRs in ai-aas-config do not have the `spec.deployment.deploymentMode` field set. The operator's reconciliation logic currently:
- Uses RawDeployment when a ModelRecipe is referenced (llama model)
- Defaults to Serverless for direct AIModel specs without recipeRef (unsloth model)

**Expected behavior**:

According to spec 030 (GPU deployment mode), GPU models should explicitly set:
```yaml
spec:
  deployment:
    deploymentMode: RawDeployment
```

**Next Actions**:

This verification confirms that ai-aas-p3xk (Update GPU recipes with explicit deploymentMode in ai-aas-config) is needed to fix the unsloth-gpt-oss-20b model configuration.

**Verification Commands Used**:
```bash
kubectl get inferenceservice -A
kubectl get inferenceservice -n development -o yaml | grep -A10 "deploymentMode\|annotations:"
kubectl get aimodel -n development -o yaml
```

title: Add app-of-apps.yaml to staging environment
description:
## Overview

Create an app-of-apps.yaml for the staging environment to manage all ArgoCD Applications automatically, matching the pattern already in place for development.

## Current State

- Development has `gitops/clusters/development/app-of-apps.yaml` that manages all apps in `gitops/clusters/development/apps/`
- Staging has `gitops/clusters/staging/apps/` directory but NO app-of-apps.yaml to manage them
- Applications in staging must be manually applied with kubectl

## Required Implementation

1. Create `gitops/clusters/staging/app-of-apps.yaml` based on development template
2. Update targetRevision to `staging` branch
3. Update path to `gitops/clusters/staging/apps`
4. Update metadata name to `staging-apps`
5. Update environment label to `staging`
6. Bootstrap with `kubectl apply -f gitops/clusters/staging/app-of-apps.yaml` on staging cluster

## Template (from development)

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: staging-apps
  namespace: argocd
  labels:
    environment: staging
    app: app-of-apps
  finalizers:
    - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/otherjamesbrown/ai-aas
    targetRevision: staging
    path: gitops/clusters/staging/apps
    directory:
      recurse: true
      exclude: '{network/**,observability/**,secrets/**,cert-manager/**}'
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: argocd
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
      allowEmpty: false
    syncOptions:
      - CreateNamespace=false
      - PrunePropagationPolicy=foreground
    retry:
      limit: 5
      backoff:
        duration: 5s
        factor: 2
        maxDuration: 3m
```

## Files to Create

- `gitops/clusters/staging/app-of-apps.yaml`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] File exists at `gitops/clusters/staging/app-of-apps.yaml`
- [ ] targetRevision is set to `staging`
- [ ] path points to `gitops/clusters/staging/apps`
- [ ] App is bootstrapped on staging cluster
- [ ] All applications in staging/apps/ are automatically synced

## Related Issues

- ai-aas-2m7: Implement ArgoCD App-of-Apps pattern for environment management (parent task)

gpt-oss model requires special vLLM build (0.10.1+gptoss)
description:
The gpt-oss-20b model has a custom 'gpt_oss' architecture that is not supported by standard vLLM builds. According to vLLM documentation, you need a special pre-release build: vllm==0.10.1+gptoss from https://wheels.vllm.ai/gpt-oss/

The error is: ValueError: The checkpoint you are trying to load has model type 'gpt_oss' but Transformers does not recognize this architecture.

Options to fix:
1. Build a custom vLLM Docker image with the gpt-oss wheel
2. Wait for gpt-oss support to be merged into mainline vLLM
3. Use a different model that works with standard vLLM (like Mistral, Llama, etc.)

Note: This is NOT a trust_remote_code issue - the model doesn't have custom Python files. It's an architecture support issue.

Related: https://docs.unsloth.ai/models/gpt-oss-how-to-run-and-fine-tune

comments.author: dev

title: Step 6: Make downloader and runtime images configurable
description:
## Task

Make the downloader and vLLM images configurable via environment variables or controller flags instead of being hardcoded.

**File**: `operators/ai-model-operator/controllers/aimodel_controller.go`

### Current Hardcoded Values

```go
const (
    DefaultDownloaderImage = "python:3.11-slim"  // Line ~50
    // vLLM image hardcoded in vllmDeployment() or inferenceService()
)
```

### Desired Configurable Values

```go
type AIModelReconciler struct {
    client.Client
    Scheme *runtime.Scheme
    
    // Configurable via environment or flags
    DownloaderImage string  // Default: "python:3.11-slim" or custom image
    VLLMRuntime     string  // Default: "kserve-vllm" (KServe ServingRuntime name)
}
```

### Configuration Sources

1. **Environment variables** (recommended for Helm):
```yaml
# Helm values
env:
  - name: DOWNLOADER_IMAGE
    value: "ghcr.io/ai-aas/model-downloader:v1.0.0"
  - name: VLLM_RUNTIME
    value: "kserve-vllm"
```

2. **Controller flags**:
```go
// main.go
downloaderImage := flag.String("downloader-image", "python:3.11-slim", "Image for model downloader")
vllmRuntime := flag.String("vllm-runtime", "kserve-vllm", "KServe ServingRuntime for vLLM")
```

3. **ConfigMap**:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: ai-model-operator-config
data:
  DOWNLOADER_IMAGE: "ghcr.io/ai-aas/model-downloader:v1.0.0"
  VLLM_RUNTIME: "kserve-vllm"
```

### Usage in Controller

```go
func (r *AIModelReconciler) modelDownloaderJob(aimodel *aimodelv1alpha1.AIModel) *batchv1.Job {
    image := r.DownloaderImage
    if image == "" {
        image = os.Getenv("DOWNLOADER_IMAGE")
    }
    if image == "" {
        image = "python:3.11-slim"
    }
    // ...
}
```

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Downloader image configurable via env var
- [ ] Runtime selection uses configurable value
- [ ] Helm chart exposes these as values
- [ ] Default values maintained for backward compatibility

title: Implement ArgoCD App-of-Apps pattern for environment management
description:
## Overview

Implement the App-of-Apps pattern across all environments. Development already has this pattern implemented; staging and production need the same.

## Current State

| Environment | App-of-Apps | Status |
|-------------|-------------|--------|
| Development | ✅ `gitops/clusters/development/app-of-apps.yaml` | Implemented |
| Staging | ❌ Missing | Needs creation |
| Production | ❌ Missing | Needs creation |

## What is App-of-Apps?

The App-of-Apps pattern uses a single ArgoCD Application to manage all other Applications in an environment. This means:
- Adding/removing Applications is done via git commits
- No manual `kubectl apply` needed for new Applications
- Changes are automatically synced by ArgoCD

## Subtasks

1. **ai-aas-1zu**: Create `gitops/clusters/staging/app-of-apps.yaml`
2. **NEW**: Create `gitops/clusters/production/app-of-apps.yaml`

## Implementation Details

For each environment, create an app-of-apps.yaml that:
- Targets the appropriate branch (develop/staging/main)
- Points to the `apps/` directory in that environment
- Uses automated sync with prune and selfHeal
- Excludes non-Application directories (network, observability, secrets, cert-manager)

## Bootstrap Process

After creating each file:
```bash
# Staging

title: InferenceService uses raw --model=s3:// which vLLM cannot parse
description:
## Problem

The ai-model-operator creates InferenceService resources with raw container specs that pass `--model=s3://bucket/key` directly to vLLM. However, vLLM does not understand S3 URLs - it expects either a local path or a HuggingFace model ID.

### Error
```
huggingface_hub.errors.HFValidationError: Repo id must be in the form 'repo_name' or 'namespace/repo_name': 's3://ai-aas/models/gpt-oss-20b-test'. Use `repo_type` argument if needed.
```

## Root Cause

In `internal/kserve/inferenceservice.go:185`, the builder passes:
```go
args = append(args, fmt.Sprintf("--model=%s", b.modelID))
```

Where `modelID` is `s3://bucket/key`.

## Working Example

The `gpt-oss-20b-development` InferenceService (created by CLI) uses KServe's native model serving:
```yaml
spec:
  predictor:
    model:
      storageUri: s3://ai-aas/models/gpt-oss-20b/main/
      runtime: vllm-gpt-oss-runtime
```

KServe's storage initializer handles downloading from S3 to a local path before starting the container.

## Solution Options

1. **Use KServe storageUri**: Change the builder to use `spec.predictor.model.storageUri` instead of raw container args
2. **Use KServe storage initializer**: Configure the InferenceService to use KServe's built-in S3 support
3. **Download to local path first**: The model is already in S3, but vLLM needs it mounted locally

## Files to Modify

- `operators/ai-model-operator/internal/kserve/inferenceservice.go`
- `operators/ai-model-operator/controllers/aimodel_controller.go`

title: Fix bootstrap_argocd.sh to apply all ArgoCD applications

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
Root cause analysis from ai-aas-fyt/ai-aas-okp investigation:

**Problem**: Staging environment was missing KServe, Istio, Knative, and cert-manager infrastructure.

**Why it happened**: 
- scripts/gitops/bootstrap_argocd.sh only applies infrastructure-appset.yaml
- It does NOT apply individual app manifests from gitops/clusters/<env>/apps/
- Development works because it uses app-of-apps.yaml pattern (auto-discovery)
- Staging uses explicit manifest pattern but bootstrap script doesn't apply them

**What needs to change**:
Option A: Update bootstrap_argocd.sh to apply all apps:
```bash
kubectl apply -f "$APPS_DIR" --recursive
```

Option B: Add check for app-of-apps pattern:
```bash
if [ -f "$APPS_DIR/app-of-apps.yaml" ]; then
  kubectl apply -f "$APPS_DIR/app-of-apps.yaml"
else
  kubectl apply -f "$APPS_DIR" --recursive
fi
```

**Impact if not fixed**: Every new environment bootstrapped with this script will be missing infrastructure components.

title: CLI: Fix hardcoded main revision in model library commands
description:
## Problem

The model library commands have hardcoded "main" revision in S3 paths, which prevents using specific model revisions (e.g., tags, commit hashes).

## Affected Code

In `services/ai-aas-cli/cmd/model/library_cmd.go`:

```go
// Line 207
manifestPath := fmt.Sprintf("models/%s/main/.manifest.json", m.Name)

// Line 408
storageURI := fmt.Sprintf("s3://%s/models/%s/main/", s3Bucket, modelName)

// Line 709
storageURI := fmt.Sprintf("s3://%s/models/%s/main/", s3Bucket, enableModel)

// Line 734
rollbackCfg.StorageURI = fmt.Sprintf("s3://%s/models/%s/main/", s3Bucket, disableModel)
```

## Impact

- Cannot deploy specific model versions (e.g., `v1.0`, commit SHA)
- All deployments use "main" regardless of what was cached
- Breaks versioned model workflow

## Required Fix

1. **Model registry should track revision**
   - Store revision in model registry DB
   - Default to "main" if not specified

2. **Library commands should use stored revision**
   ```go
   storageURI := fmt.Sprintf("s3://%s/models/%s/%s/", s3Bucket, modelName, model.Revision)
   ```

3. **Add --revision flag to enable command**
   ```bash
   ai-aas-cli model library enable mistral-7b --revision v1.0
   ```

## Files to Modify

- `services/ai-aas-cli/cmd/model/library_cmd.go` - Fix hardcoded paths
- `services/admin-api-service/internal/models/model.go` - Add Revision field if missing
- `db/migrations/` - Add revision column to models table if needed

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] library enable uses model's cached revision
- [ ] library disable references correct revision
- [ ] manifest lookup uses correct revision path
- [ ] Default to "main" when revision not specified
- [ ] --revision flag added to enable command

rollback-test:

title: Investigate incomplete memory limit rollout
description:
The memory limit fix (32Gi → 24Gi) has not fully resolved benchmark failures.

## Root Cause Identified
Old 32Gi pods (revision 00001) are STILL running alongside new 24Gi pods. Traffic is split between them, so when old pods OOM-restart, requests fail.

## Current Pod State
| Model | Old Pod (32Gi) | Restarts | New Pod (24Gi) |
|-------|----------------|----------|----------------|
| mistral-7b | Running (00001) | 367 | Running (00130) |
| openai-gpt-oss-20b | Running (00001) | 374 | Running (00146) |
| unsloth-gpt-oss-20b | Running (00001) | 425 | NONE |

## InferenceService Config
All 3 InferenceServices now show 24Gi (config applied correctly).

## Why Rollout Stuck?
KServe rolling update is not completing - old revisions not being terminated.
Possible causes:
1. Traffic not shifting to new revisions
2. GPU resource constraints preventing new pods from fully starting
3. KServe revision garbage collection not working

## Suggested Fix
Manually delete old revision deployments to force traffic to new pods:
```
kubectl delete deployment -n development -l serving.knative.dev/revision=mistral-7b-instruct-v03-predictor-00001
kubectl delete deployment -n development -l serving.knative.dev/revision=openai-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001  
kubectl delete deployment -n development -l serving.knative.dev/revision=unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001
```

## Related
- Original OOM investigation: INVESTIGATION_REPORT_ai-aas-vju2.md
- Config commit: febe54a in ai-aas-config repo

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Investigation Complete

Root cause identified in investigation **ai-aas-1ekm**.

**Summary**: NOT a KServe/Knative bug. This is a GitOps configuration conflict.

Two ArgoCD Applications manage the same AIModel resources:
- `aimodels-development` (ai-aas repo) with STALE 32Gi config
- `aimodels-config-development` (ai-aas-config repo) with NEW 24Gi config

This creates a race condition where the stale config wins, causing:
1. New pods request 32Gi memory (exceeds node capacity)
2. New pods cannot schedule (Insufficient memory)
3. Traffic stuck on old pods (only ready pods)
4. Knative GC cannot delete old pods (they're active)
5. System stuck in rollout deadlock

**Fix**: Delete the duplicate `aimodels-development` ArgoCD Application

**Full details**: /home/dev/ai-aas/INVESTIGATION_REPORT_ai-aas-1ekm.md

**Fix bead**: ai-aas-7hek

title: Implement automatic routing policy and model access control
description:
## Summary
Implement automatic routing policy creation and user-level model access control based on findings from ai-aas-5ht.

## Root Cause (from investigation)
- Staging has **0 routing policies** despite models being registered
- Auto-creation code exists but is not working (silently failing or not being called)
- Users default to 'restricted' mode with no model grants

## Technical Tasks

### Task 1: Fix Routing Policy Auto-Creation (CRITICAL)
**Files:**
- `services/admin-api-service/internal/service/registry.go`

**Changes:**
1. Debug why `createDefaultRoutingPolicy` is failing in staging
2. Check if `policyRepo` is being passed correctly during initialization
3. Add better error logging to surface failures
4. Consider making policy creation failure a hard error (not just warning)

**Verification:**
- Register a new model → routing policy should be auto-created

### Task 2: Org Admin Auto-Grant Model Access
**Files:**
- `services/user-org-service/internal/httpapi/users/handlers.go`
- `services/user-org-service/internal/storage/postgres/model_access.go`

**Changes:**
1. In `CreateUser()`, after user creation, check if roles include 'admin'
2. If admin role, call `SetUserAccessMode(ctx, orgID, userID, "auto_grant")`
3. This ensures Org Admins automatically have access to all models

**Example:**
```go
// After user creation in CreateUser()
if containsRole(req.Roles, "admin") {
    _, err := h.runtime.Postgres.SetUserAccessMode(ctx, orgID, createdUser.ID, "auto_grant")
    if err != nil {
        h.logger.Warn("failed to set auto_grant for admin user", zap.Error(err))
    }
}
```

### Task 3: CLI Support for User Access Mode
**Files:**
- `services/ai-aas-cli/cmd/user/create.go`

**Changes:**
1. Add `--model-access` flag with options: `all` or `restricted`
2. Default to `restricted` for non-admin users
3. Default to `all` (auto_grant) for admin users

### Task 4: Create Missing Staging Routing Policies (Immediate Fix)
**Action:**
- Use Admin API to create routing policies for existing staging models
- This is a workaround until auto-creation is fixed

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://admin-api.staging.otherjamesbrown.com/v1/routing/policies' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <staging-key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "organization_id": "*",
    "model": "mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3",
    "backends": [{"backend_id": "mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3", "weight": 100}],
    "failover_threshold": 3
  }'
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New model registration auto-creates global routing policy
- [ ] Smoke test passes on staging (no 'routing policy configured' error)
- [ ] New users with 'admin' role get auto_grant access mode
- [ ] Non-admin users can be created with 'all' or 'restricted' access
- [ ] CLI supports `--model-access` flag for user creation

title: Investigate routing policy system and model access control
description:
## Context
Staging smoke test fails with 'no routing policy configured' error when calling inference on mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3.

## Investigation Findings

### Root Cause Analysis

**FINDING 1: Staging has NO routing policies**
- Development has 2 policies (for `mistral-7b` and `gpt-oss-20b`)
- Staging has 0 policies
- The model is registered but no routing policy exists for it

**FINDING 2: Auto-creation of routing policies IS implemented** (but has issues)
The code in `services/admin-api-service/internal/service/registry.go:58-69` already implements auto-creation:
```go
// Auto-create global routing policy for new models (default behavior)
if created && s.policyRepo \!= nil {
    if err := s.createDefaultRoutingPolicy(ctx, model); err \!= nil {
        // Log the error but don't fail the registration
        s.logger.Warn("failed to auto-create routing policy", ...)
    }
}
```

**FINDING 3: Model name mismatch in development**
- Policy uses: `mistral-7b`, `gpt-oss-20b`
- Actual models: `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3`, `unsloth/gpt-oss-20b`
- This works because the routing engine uses the backend_id which correctly maps to the model

**FINDING 4: User Access Control IS implemented** (Spec 022)
User model access already exists with two modes:
- `auto_grant`: User can access ALL models (default for service accounts)
- `restricted`: User can only access explicitly granted models

The implementation is in:
- `user-org-service/internal/storage/postgres/model_access.go`
- `user-org-service/internal/httpapi/auth/validate_api_key.go`
- `api-router-service/internal/auth/authenticator.go`

**FINDING 5: Default access mode is 'restricted' (fail-closed)**
When a new user is created:
- No `user_model_access` record exists
- Default is 'restricted' mode
- No models are granted
- User has access to 0 models

### Current Architecture

```
Routing Policy Flow:
Admin API → routing_policies table → API Router sync → Cache

User Access Flow:
API Key → User-Org validate → ModelAccessMode + GrantedModels → API Router checks CanAccessModel()
```

### Gaps Identified

| # | Gap | Current State | Expected State |
|---|-----|---------------|----------------|
| 1 | No auto-creation of routing policies in staging | Policies manually created | Auto-create on model registration |
| 2 | User default is 'restricted' with no grants | New users have 0 model access | Org Admins should have 'auto_grant' |
| 3 | No role-based auto_grant | Roles stored in metadata only | 'admin' role should trigger auto_grant |
| 4 | No way to set 'all models' access for non-admins | Only restricted+grants or auto_grant | Need 'all_models' user flag |

### Technical Changes Needed

**1. Fix: Model Registration → Routing Policy Auto-creation**
- Investigate why staging doesn't have policies
- Ensure `createDefaultRoutingPolicy` is called and succeeds
- Check if policyRepo is nil or if there's a database issue

**2. Enhancement: Org Admin Auto-Grant**
- When user is created with 'admin' role → set `access_mode = 'auto_grant'`
- Location: `user-org-service/internal/httpapi/users/handlers.go:CreateUser()`

**3. Enhancement: User Access Modes**
Current modes:
- `restricted`: Only explicitly granted models
- `auto_grant`: All models with routing policies

Proposed modes:
- `restricted`: Only explicitly granted models (snapshot)
- `all_models`: All current and future models (dynamic like auto_grant)
- `admin` role implies `all_models`

**4. No Changes Needed: Routing is already global**
- Policies already use `organization_id = "*"` for global policies
- No org-level routing policy restriction exists

## Deliverables
- [x] Document current routing policy architecture
- [x] Identify gaps between current state and expected functionality
- [x] List specific code changes needed
- [ ] Create implementation plan for ai-aas-5ge

title: Investigate: api-router-service startup hang after DATABASE_URL added
close_reason: Implemented Option B: removed direct database access from api-router, now calls admin-api for /v1/models. Commit 4141d6ca

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Prior Investigation (from conversation)

**Symptom**: api-router-service pods hang during startup and never reach HTTP server start. Startup probe kills container after ~60 seconds.

**Observed Behavior**:
- Logs consistently stop at line 309 of main.go: "Kafka publisher not configured (usage tracking disabled)"
- App never reaches line 383 (model registry initialization) or line 534 (HTTP server start)
- New pods with DATABASE_URL configured are crashlooping with Exit Code 2 (startup probe failure)
- Old pods (without DATABASE_URL) were working fine

**Recent Changes**:
- Commit c11d8433: Added DATABASE_URL environment variable to api-router Helm values
- Commit ed8850ca: Added ModelRegistry code requiring database access
- Reason: /v1/models endpoint now requires database access via ModelRegistry

**Files Involved**:
- services/api-router-service/cmd/router/main.go (lines 309-534)
- services/api-router-service/internal/routing/registry.go
- services/api-router-service/deployments/helm/api-router-service/values-development.yaml

**Key Question**: Why does app hang between line 309 and line 383? Code appears to be non-blocking struct initialization.

**Architecture Question**: Should api-router connect directly to database for /v1/models, or delegate to admin-api-service?

**Database Info**:
- Akamai managed PostgreSQL
- DATABASE_URL format: postgres://user:pass@host:port/db?sslmode=require
- admin-api-service already has database access and /models endpoint

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## New Findings

**Confirmed Behavior**:
- Logs consistently stop at line 309: "Kafka publisher not configured (usage tracking disabled)"
- Pod is killed by startup probe after ~120 seconds (failureThreshold=60 * periodSeconds=2)
- Startup probe fails with "connection refused" - HTTP server never starts
- Application appears to hang between line 309 and line 383 (NewRegistry call)

**Pod Events**:
```
Warning  Unhealthy  Startup probe failed: dial tcp connect: connection refused
Normal   Killing    Container router failed startup probe, will be restarted
```

**Code Sections Between Log Lines**:
- Lines 310-332: Usage buffer store initialization (only if kafkaPublisher != nil)
- Lines 334-347: Usage hook initialization (only if kafkaPublisher != nil)
- Lines 349-356: Build metadata initialization
- Lines 358-386: Status handlers and platform health initialization
- Line 389: NewRegistry call (database connection)

**Analysis**: Since kafkaPublisher is nil (not configured), lines 314-347 should be skipped. The hang must be in status handlers (lines 358-386) or before.

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED

**Test Results**:
```bash
# TCP connection test from pod to database
timeout 5 nc -zv a383749-akamai-prod-3730350-default.g2a.akamaidb.net 11887
# Result: HUNG - timed out after 2 minutes
```

**Root Cause**: The Akamai PostgreSQL database at a383749-akamai-prod-3730350-default.g2a.akamaidb.net:11887 is **NOT REACHABLE** from the Kubernetes cluster.

**Evidence**:
1. Working pods (5b779fdb*) do NOT have DATABASE_URL env var set
2. Failing pod (557977dc*) DOES have DATABASE_URL env var set
3. TCP connection to database from pod hangs indefinitely
4. routing.NewRegistry() at line 389 of main.go calls sql.Open() then db.PingContext(ctx, 5*time.Second) at registry.go:76-80
5. The Ping should timeout after 5 seconds, but TCP connection establishment itself hangs before reaching that

**Why Application Hangs**:
- routing.NewRegistry() is called synchronously at main.go:389
- sql.Open() returns immediately (doesn't connect)
- db.PingContext() attempts actual connection
- TCP SYN packet is sent to database, no SYN-ACK received
- Connection attempt hangs at TCP layer (waiting for network timeout, typically 2+ minutes)
- HTTP server is never started (line 534)
- Startup probe fails after 120 seconds (60 * 2s)

**Network Issue**: The database is an Akamai managed PostgreSQL instance. It appears the Kubernetes cluster cannot route to this external Akamai database endpoint.

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED: NetworkPolicy Blocking External Database Access

**Definitive Root Cause**: The api-router-service NetworkPolicy blocks egress to external IPs.

**Proof**:
1. admin-api-service pod (no NetworkPolicy): CAN connect to database
   ```
   nc -zv a383749-akamai-prod-3730350-default.g2a.akamaidb.net 11887
   # Result: SUCCESS - connection open
   ```

2. api-router-service pod (has restrictive NetworkPolicy): CANNOT connect
   ```
   nc -zv a383749-akamai-prod-3730350-default.g2a.akamaidb.net 11887
   # Result: HANG - times out
   ```

**NetworkPolicy Analysis**:
- File: `gitops/clusters/development/network-policies/api-router-service.yaml`
- Egress rules allow ONLY:
  - DNS (port 53)
  - Internal Kubernetes services (etcd, redis, user-org-service, admin-api-service)
  - vLLM backends (port 8000, 8012)
  - Monitoring (port 4317)
- No egress rule for external database at 172.234.177.213:11887

**Code Path**:
1. main.go:389 - routing.NewRegistry() called synchronously
2. registry.go:70 - sql.Open("postgres", cfg.DatabaseURL)
3. registry.go:78 - db.PingContext(ctx, 5*time.Second) attempts connection
4. TCP SYN sent to 172.234.177.213:11887
5. NetworkPolicy drops packet (no matching egress rule)
6. TCP stack waits for SYN-ACK, eventually times out (2+ minutes)
7. Startup probe fails after 120s, pod killed

**Why it worked before**: Old pods don't have DATABASE_URL env var set, so NewRegistry returns early with error and doesn't block startup.

title: Make retry parameters configurable via operator flags

## Summary

Allow retry parameters to be configured via operator command-line flags or environment variables.

## Configuration Options

| Parameter | Flag | Env Var | Default |
|-----------|------|---------|---------|
| Max retries | --max-download-retries | MAX_DOWNLOAD_RETRIES | 5 |
| Initial delay | --initial-retry-delay | INITIAL_RETRY_DELAY | 1m |
| Max delay | --max-retry-delay | MAX_RETRY_DELAY | 16m |

## Changes Required

### 1. Add flags to main.go

```go
flag.IntVar(&maxDownloadRetries, "max-download-retries", 5, "Maximum download retry attempts")
flag.DurationVar(&initialRetryDelay, "initial-retry-delay", time.Minute, "Initial retry delay")
flag.DurationVar(&maxRetryDelay, "max-retry-delay", 16*time.Minute, "Maximum retry delay")
```

### 2. Pass config to reconciler

```go
type AIModelReconciler struct {
    client.Client
    Scheme            *runtime.Scheme
    MaxDownloadRetries int32
    InitialRetryDelay  time.Duration
    MaxRetryDelay      time.Duration
}
```

### 3. Update Helm chart values

Add to values.yaml:
```yaml
operator:
  maxDownloadRetries: 5
  initialRetryDelay: "1m"
  maxRetryDelay: "16m"
```

title: Update CLI smoke test to grant model access for test user
description:
## Problem
The CLI smoke test creates a user with `--roles admin` but doesn't ensure model access is granted. Once ai-aas-cl3 is implemented, admin users will auto-get `auto_grant` mode, but until then (and for robustness), the smoke test should explicitly ensure the test user has model access.

## Current Flow (scripts/cli-smoke-test.sh)
1. Create org
2. Create user with `--roles admin`
3. Activate user
4. Create API key
5. List models ← May fail if user has no model access
6. Make inference call ← Fails with 'no routing policy' or access denied

## Proposed Fix
After creating the user (step 2), add:
```bash
# Test 2.5: Grant model access to test user
run_cli user model-access set-mode \
    --org-id "$org_slug" \
    --user-id "$user_id" \
    --mode auto_grant \
    --user-org-endpoint "$user_org_endpoint" \
    --api-key "$api_key"
```

Alternatively, once ai-aas-1bp is done:
```bash
# Create user with model access
run_cli user create \
    --org-id "$org_slug" \
    --email "$user_email" \
    --roles admin \
    --model-access all \  # New flag
    ...
```

## Files to Modify
- `scripts/cli-smoke-test.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Smoke test passes even if admin auto-grant is not yet implemented
- [ ] Test user can list models and make inference calls
- [ ] Test output shows model access grant step (verbose mode)

## Dependencies
- Can be done independently (workaround)
- OR wait for ai-aas-1bp (--model-access flag) for cleaner solution

## Testing
```bash
./scripts/cli-smoke-test.sh --dev-only --verbose
# Should see model access step
# Inference call should succeed
```

Migration `20251115001_core_entities.sql` is failing in development with:
```
ERROR: column "organization_id" does not exist (SQLSTATE 42703)
```

The error occurs at:
```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_org ON users (organization_id);
```

## Root Cause

1. The `users` table already exists in the database (from user-org-service or previous migrations)
2. The existing `users` table has a **different schema** - it doesn't have the `organization_id` column
3. When goose runs the migration:
   - `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (...)` succeeds (table exists, skips creation)
   - `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_org ON users (organization_id)` fails (column doesn't exist)

This happened because:
- Migration files were renamed from `.up.sql` to `.sql` (goose v2 → v3 format)
- Goose may see the new filename as an unapplied migration
- The database was set up with a different schema initially

## Current State

- Pod `admin-api-service-development-748bb4557b-f4qhb` is in Init:CrashLoopBackOff
- Old pod `admin-api-service-development-ddc44666c-87n88` is still running (migrations disabled)

## Required Fix

Make migrations truly idempotent by:

1. **Check column existence before creating indexes:**
```sql
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns 
             WHERE table_name = 'users' AND column_name = 'organization_id') THEN
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_org ON users (organization_id);
  END IF;
END $$;
```

2. **Or use dynamic SQL to handle schema differences**

3. **Or add columns if they don't exist:**
```sql
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns 
                 WHERE table_name = 'users' AND column_name = 'organization_id') THEN
    ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN organization_id UUID;
  END IF;
END $$;
```

## Files to Update

- `db/migrations/operational/20251115001_core_entities.sql` - Main failing migration
- Potentially other migrations with similar patterns

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Migrations run successfully on fresh database
- [ ] Migrations run successfully on database with existing tables (different schema)
- [ ] Pod starts without Init:CrashLoopBackOff
- [ ] goose_db_version table is correctly updated

## Related

- ai-aas-fo4: Migration format conversion (closed - caused this issue)
- ai-aas-v2b: Model rename endpoint (closed - unblocked but deployment affected)

comments.author: dev

## Context Gap Found

Investigation ai-aas-1ekm revealed missing anti-pattern in `context/infra-ops-manager/agents.md`.

## What to Add

### Anti-pattern: Duplicate ArgoCD Applications

```yaml
# WRONG: Two ArgoCD Applications managing same resources
---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: aimodels-development
spec:
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/org/ai-aas
    path: infra/k8s/aimodels/development
---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: aimodels-config-development
spec:
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/org/ai-aas-config
    path: environments/development/models
# Both manage the same AIModel CRs → SharedResourceWarning → config drift
```

### How to Detect

```bash
kubectl get applications -A -o yaml | grep SharedResourceWarning
```

### Why Dangerous

- Race condition: both apps sync continuously
- Config drift: conflicting values fight for control
- Unpredictable state: last sync wins
- Rollout deadlock: operators see changing spec

### How to Fix

1. Delete one ArgoCD Application
2. Keep single source of truth
3. Use Helm with remote values or Kustomize with remote bases if need multi-repo

title: Evaluate migration to 100% Istio ingress (remove NGINX)
description:
## Background

Currently the platform uses a dual-ingress architecture:
- **NGINX Ingress**: Primary for all service ingress (external HTTP/HTTPS traffic)
- **Istio**: Only for KServe/Knative internal routing (knative-local-gateway)

Since Istio is already required for KServe, we should evaluate whether consolidating to 100% Istio makes sense.

## Current State

| Component | Development | Staging |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| NGINX Ingress | 172.232.58.222 | 172.236.135.55 |
| Istio Ingress | 172.232.48.93 | 172.236.132.56 |

Services using NGINX: api-router, admin-api, user-org, analytics, web-portal, etcd, grafana, loki, argocd

## Pros of 100% Istio

1. **Single ingress system** - less operational complexity
2. **Unified observability** - distributed tracing, metrics across ALL services
3. **mTLS everywhere** - automatic encryption between services
4. **Advanced traffic management** - circuit breaking, retries, fault injection, canary deployments
5. **Consistent patterns** - same Gateway/VirtualService config everywhere

## Cons of 100% Istio

1. **Resource overhead** - Envoy sidecar per pod (~50m CPU, 128Mi RAM)
2. **Complexity** - steeper learning curve, harder debugging
3. **Migration effort** - rewrite all Ingress resources to Gateway/VirtualService
4. **Verbose config** - Istio Gateway + VirtualService vs simple Ingress

## Investigation Tasks

### 1. Resource Impact Assessment
- [ ] Calculate current resource usage without sidecars
- [ ] Estimate additional resources with Istio sidecars on all pods
- [ ] Determine if cluster can handle the overhead

### 2. Feature Requirements Analysis
- [ ] List services that would benefit from service mesh features
- [ ] Identify any services that should NOT have sidecars (performance-critical)
- [ ] Evaluate mTLS requirements for compliance/security

### 3. Migration Complexity
- [ ] Audit all current Ingress resources
- [ ] Create sample Gateway/VirtualService equivalents
- [ ] Estimate migration effort per service
- [ ] Identify breaking changes or incompatibilities

### 4. Operational Readiness
- [ ] Assess team familiarity with Istio
- [ ] Document debugging/troubleshooting procedures
- [ ] Evaluate monitoring/alerting changes needed

### 5. Decision & Recommendation
- [ ] Write ADR (Architecture Decision Record) with recommendation
- [ ] If approved, create detailed migration plan
- [ ] If rejected, document reasons and close this issue

## Blocked By

- ai-aas-ir7: Standardize current ingress architecture first (get NGINX into GitOps before potentially removing it)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Clear recommendation (migrate or stay) with justification
- [ ] If migrate: detailed plan with resource estimates and timeline
- [ ] ADR documented in docs/architecture/decisions/

title: Create docs/platform/istio-integration.md
Add GPU Large node pool for TensorRT-LLM workloads
T020 Verify pods scheduled to GPU nodes
GPU Operator NFD workers blocked by gpu-workload taint on staging
description:
## Problem

The GPU Operator's Node Feature Discovery (NFD) workers cannot run on the GPU nodes in the staging cluster, preventing GPU discovery and driver installation.

## Root Cause

GPU nodes have a custom taint:
```
gpu-workload=true:NoSchedule
```

But the NFD workers only tolerate:
```
nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule
```

This prevents NFD pods from being scheduled on GPU nodes.

## Impact

- ClusterPolicy status: "No GPU node found"
- NVIDIA drivers not installed on GPU nodes
- Device plugin not deployed
- `nvidia.com/gpu` resource not available for scheduling
- **Blocks all model deployments to staging**

## Affected Nodes

- `lke541701-785977-504f85d60000` (RTX 4000 Ada)
- `lke541701-785978-0670819e0000` (RTX 4000 Ada)

## Solution

Add toleration for `gpu-workload` taint to the GPU operator ArgoCD application:

```yaml
node-feature-discovery:
  worker:
    tolerations:
      - key: "gpu-workload"
        operator: "Equal"
        value: "true"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
      - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
        operator: "Exists"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
```

Alternative: Remove the custom `gpu-workload` taint and rely on the standard `nvidia.com/gpu` taint that gets auto-applied by the GPU operator after discovery.

## Verification

After fix, verify:
1. NFD workers running on GPU nodes: `kubectl get pods -n gpu-operator -o wide`
2. ClusterPolicy ready: `kubectl get clusterpolicy -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status}'`
3. GPU resources available: `kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[].status.allocatable["nvidia.com/gpu"]'`

title: vLLM backend (llama-3.1-8b-instruct) timing out after NetworkPolicy fix
close_reason: INVESTIGATED: Root cause identified as NetworkPolicy port mismatch (config_drift). NetworkPolicy allows egress to ports 8000 and 9000, but TRT-LLM backend listens on port 8080. Fix bead created: ai-aas-3vdx assigned to infra-ops-manager.

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Prior Investigation (from conversation)

**Symptom**: vLLM backend for llama-3.1-8b-instruct timing out after 30 seconds on inference requests

**Already Tried**:
- Applied NetworkPolicy fix adding egress rules for ports 8000 (HTTP) and 9000 (gRPC) to pods with serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice label
- Result: Triton backend (gpt-oss-20b on port 9000) started working immediately (668ms response)
- Result: vLLM backend (llama-3.1-8b-instruct on port 8000) still times out after 30s

**Working vs Broken**:
- ✅ gpt-oss-20b (Triton/gRPC on port 9000): Working - 668ms response
- ❌ llama-3.1-8b-instruct (vLLM on port 8000): Timeout after 30s

**Files Examined**:
- infra/k8s/network-policies/development/api-router-policy.yaml - NetworkPolicy with egress rules

**Hypotheses to Test**:
1. vLLM pod might not have the serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice label (it's a RawDeployment, not KServe)
2. vLLM might be listening on a different port than configured
3. vLLM pod might not be running or healthy
4. Backend endpoint configuration might be wrong for vLLM

**Environment**:
- Kubeconfig: /home/dev/kubeconfigs/kubeconfig-development.yaml
- NetworkPolicy: infra/k8s/network-policies/development/api-router-policy.yaml

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Key Finding

**ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED**: NetworkPolicy port mismatch

The api-router is connecting to the Service on port 80:
- Backend config: http://llama-3-1-8b-instruct-trtllm-predictor.development.svc.cluster.local:80

The Service maps port 80 → targetPort 8080, and the pod listens on:
- Port 8080 (HTTP)
- Port 9000 (gRPC)
- Port 8002 (metrics)

The NetworkPolicy only allows egress to ports 8000 and 9000 for pods with serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice label, but NOT port 80.

When api-router tries to connect to the Service on port 80, the NetworkPolicy blocks it because port 80 is not in the allowed egress list.

**Why Triton works**: The gpt-oss-20b backend likely uses port 9000 directly, which IS allowed by the NetworkPolicy.

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Investigation Complete

**Evidence Gathered**:

| Source | Finding |
|--------|---------|
| Backend config | meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct → http://llama-3-1-8b-instruct-trtllm-predictor.development.svc.cluster.local:80 |
| Service | Port 80 → targetPort 8080 |
| Pod | Listens on ports 8080 (HTTP), 9000 (gRPC), 8002 (metrics) |
| Pod labels | serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice: llama-3-1-8b-instruct-trtllm |
| NetworkPolicy | Allows egress to ports 8000 and 9000 ONLY |
| Connection test | Timeout when connecting from api-router pod to llama service port 80 |
| Connection test | Timeout when connecting from api-router pod to llama service port 8080 |

**Hypotheses Tested**:

| Hypothesis | Verdict | Evidence |
|------------|---------|----------|
| vLLM pod missing label | ❌ Ruled out | Pod has serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice label |
| vLLM on different port | ✅ CONFIRMED | Pod listens on 8080, not 8000 |
| vLLM pod not running | ❌ Ruled out | Pod is Running (1/1) |
| NetworkPolicy blocking port 80/8080 | ✅ CONFIRMED | Connection tests timeout |

**Comparison with Working Backend**:

| Backend | Service Port | Target Port | Pod Port | NetworkPolicy Allows? |
|---------|-------------|-------------|----------|----------------------|
| gpt-oss-20b (Triton) | 80 | 8000 | 8000 | ✅ Port 8000 allowed |
| llama-3.1-8b (TRT-LLM) | 80 | 8080 | 8080 | ❌ Port 8080 NOT allowed |

**Root Cause**: NetworkPolicy allows egress to ports 8000 and 9000, but the llama-3.1-8b-instruct pod listens on port 8080. The service maps port 80 → 8080, but NetworkPolicy blocks traffic to port 8080.

title: Audit all CLI commands for profile support consistency
description:
## Problem

The CLI `-p <profile>` / `--profile <profile>` flag doesn't work for most commands. Commands use `config.Load()` which doesn't apply profile overrides, instead of `config.GetEffectiveConfig(profileName)` which properly merges profile settings.

## Impact

- Users cannot use named profiles with commands like `model registry list`
- Must manually edit top-level config values as a workaround
- Profile system is essentially broken for core functionality

## Root Cause

Commands in `cmd/model/registry.go` and other files call:
```go
cfg, err := config.Load()
```

But should call:
```go
cfg, _, err := config.GetEffectiveConfig(profileFlag)
```

Where `profileFlag` comes from the `-p` flag value.

## Affected Commands

- `model registry list`
- `model registry add`
- `model registry info`
- `model registry remove`
- `model registry status`
- `model registry rename`
- Likely many other commands

## Solution

1. Update all commands to use `GetEffectiveConfig()` instead of `Load()`
2. Pass the profile flag value from cobra to the config loader
3. Consider creating a helper function that commands can call consistently

## Testing

```bash
# Create a profile
ai-aas-cli profile create test-profile \
  --admin-api-endpoint=https://admin-api.dev.otherjamesbrown.com

# Manually add api_key to profile in ~/.ai-aas-cli.yaml

# This should work but currently fails:
ai-aas-cli model registry list -p test-profile
```

5. Knative GC will delete old revisions

## Context Update Needed

**File**: `docs/runbooks/build-tensorrt-llm-engine.md`

**Root Cause Bead**: ai-aas-zhlx

**What's Missing**: 
The runbook shows correct relative paths in examples but doesn't validate that builds actually produce relative paths. Some build processes may generate absolute paths that work locally but fail in production.

**Add Section** (after Step 5, before Step 6 Upload to S3):

```markdown
### Step 5.5: Validate Path Configuration

**CRITICAL**: Before uploading to S3, verify no hardcoded absolute paths exist.

```bash
# Check for hardcoded paths from build environment
cd model_repository
grep -r '/workspace' .
grep -r '/opt/' . | grep -v '#'  # Exclude comments

# Should return NOTHING. If found, fix before upload.

# Common issues:
# 1. preprocessing/1/model.py - hardcoded tokenizer path
# 2. postprocessing/1/model.py - hardcoded tokenizer path

# Correct patterns:
# - Use args['model_repository'] for relative paths
# - Use /mnt/models for runtime paths (NOT /workspace)
```

**Why this matters**: 
- Build environment uses `/workspace/` paths
- Runtime environment mounts to `/mnt/models`
- Hardcoded build paths cause immediate pod crashes
```

comments.text:
## Evidence #1: API Router Logs

**Finding**: API router is attempting to connect to wrong service DNS names

**Examples from logs**:
- Looking for: `openai-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private.development.svc.cluster.local`
- Looking for: `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-...` (note: logs show it tries this too)

**Actual service that exists**:
- `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private` (in development namespace)
- `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00002-private` (in development namespace)

**Error**: `dial tcp: lookup <wrong-service-name> on 10.128.0.10:53: no such host`

**Hypothesis**: Model name mismatch between what CLI requests and what service names exist in cluster.

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Evidence #2: API Router Configuration vs Reality

**API Router BACKEND_ENDPOINTS env var**:
```
unsloth/gpt-oss-20b:http://unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private.development.svc.cluster.local:8012
openai/gpt-oss-20b:http://openai-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private.development.svc.cluster.local:8012
mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3:http://mistral-7b-instruct-v03-predictor-00001-private.development.svc.cluster.local:8012
```

**Actual InferenceService in cluster**:
- Name: `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b` (READY, in development namespace)
- Active revision: `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00002` (not 00001!)

**Problem identified**:
1. API router is configured to route to `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private`
2. But the active revision is now `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00002-private`
3. The `00001` service no longer exists (or is not active)
4. DNS lookup fails → 502 BACKEND_ERROR

**Additional issue**:
- There's also an `openai/gpt-oss-20b` entry that points to a non-existent service
- Multiple model name prefixes configured for same backend (unsloth/, openai/)

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Root Cause Identified

**Category**: `config_drift`

**Explanation**:
The API router's `BACKEND_ENDPOINTS` environment variable contains hardcoded service DNS names that reference specific KServe revision numbers (e.g., `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private`). When KServe rolls out a new revision (00002), the old revision number in the config becomes stale.

**Flow of the bug**:
1. CLI requests model `gpt-oss-20b` (no prefix)
2. API router rewrites it to `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (line 153 in openai.go)
3. Looks up backend endpoint for `openai/gpt-oss-20b` from BACKEND_ENDPOINTS env var
4. Finds: `http://openai-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private.development.svc.cluster.local:8012`
5. Attempts DNS lookup for this service
6. DNS fails because:
   - The service `openai-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private` does NOT exist
   - Only `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private` and `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00002-private` exist
7. Returns 502 BACKEND_ERROR to CLI

**Two problems**:
1. **Wrong model prefix**: Config has `openai/gpt-oss-20b` but actual service is `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b`
2. **Hardcoded revision numbers**: Pointing to `00001` but active revision is `00002`

**Evidence**:
- BACKEND_ENDPOINTS env var: `openai/gpt-oss-20b:http://openai-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private...`
- Actual InferenceService: `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b` with active revision `00002`
- API router logs: `dial tcp: lookup openai-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00001-private... no such host`

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## Proposed Fix

**High-level description**:

**Immediate fix** (line 128 in values-development.yaml):
1. Remove the invalid `openai/gpt-oss-20b` entry (service doesn't exist)
2. Update `unsloth/gpt-oss-20b` to use revision-agnostic DNS name OR update to 00002

**Option A - Revision-agnostic** (RECOMMENDED):
```yaml
backends:
  endpoints: "unsloth/gpt-oss-20b:http://unsloth-gpt-oss-20b.development.svc.cluster.local:80,..."
```
Uses KServe's public ExternalName service which routes to the active revision automatically.

**Option B - Update to 00002**:
```yaml
backends:
  endpoints: "unsloth/gpt-oss-20b:http://unsloth-gpt-oss-20b-predictor-00002-private.development.svc.cluster.local:8012,..."
```
This will break again on next revision rollout.

**Root cause prevention**:
- BACKEND_ENDPOINTS should not hardcode KServe revision numbers
- Use the InferenceService name (e.g., `unsloth-gpt-oss-20b`) which routes to active revision
- Alternative: Dynamic service discovery via Admin API sync

**Affected files**:
- `services/api-router-service/deployments/helm/api-router-service/values-development.yaml` - line 128

**Estimated complexity**: Low (1-line config change)

## ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED

**Error found when manually running guidellm**:
```
httpx.HTTPStatusError: Client error '401 Unauthorized' for url 'https://api.dev.otherjamesbrown.com/v1/chat/completions/health'

**Root Cause**: 
guidellm performs backend validation BEFORE running benchmarks by calling `<target_url>/health`. In this case:

- Validation URL: https://api.dev.otherjamesbrown.com/v1/chat/completions/health
- This returns 401 Unauthorized
- guidellm silently fails validation and exits with 0 requests sent

The guidellm-runner Go wrapper likely catches the error but doesn't log it at the configured log level (info). It just reports "benchmark completed" with 0 requests.

**Category**: `config_drift` or `missing_api_endpoint`

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
## INVESTIGATION COMPLETE

# Investigation Report

**Bead**: ai-aas-82n1
**Date**: 2025-12-14
**Investigator**: debugger agent

## Symptom

guidellm-runner pod is running and appears healthy, but all benchmark runs complete with:
- 0 requests sent
- 0 successful responses
- 0 failed responses
- 0 tokens generated

## Reproduction

1. guidellm-runner runs every 5 minutes (183 runs over 15h)
2. Each run completes in ~1-3 seconds with no results
3. Pod logs show no errors, just "benchmark completed" messages

## Evidence Gathered

| Source | Finding |
|--------|---------|
| Pod logs | No errors logged, clean startup, benchmarks run on schedule |
| Prometheus metrics | `guidellm_benchmark_runs_total=183`, `guidellm_requests_total=0` |
| Manual test | guidellm CLI exits with 401 error on validation |
| Error message | `Client error '401 Unauthorized' for url 'https://api.dev.otherjamesbrown.com/v1/chat/completions/health'` |
| API testing | All /health endpoints require X-API-Key header |

## Hypotheses Tested

| Hypothesis | Verdict | Evidence |
|------------|---------|----------|
| Runner not starting | ❌ Ruled out | Pod is Running, 15h uptime, 183 benchmark runs completed |
| Configuration issue | ✅ CONFIRMED | guidellm backend validation fails with 401 |
| Backend services down | ❌ Ruled out | API is responding (returns 401, not timeout) |
| No errors being logged | ✅ CONFIRMED | guidellm-runner wrapper suppresses validation errors |

## Root Cause

**Category**: `missing_api_endpoint` + `logging_gap`

**Explanation**: 
guidellm performs backend validation before running benchmarks by making a health check request to `<target_url>/health`. The configured target is `https://api.dev.otherjamesbrown.com/v1/chat/completions`, so guidellm tries to access:

`https://api.dev.otherjamesbrown.com/v1/chat/completions/health`

This endpoint returns 401 Unauthorized because:
1. The api-router service requires authentication on ALL endpoints (including /health)
2. guidellm's validation request doesn't include the API key header
3. The validation fails, causing guidellm to exit before sending any benchmark requests

**Why silent failure**:
The guidellm-runner Go wrapper catches the error but doesn't log it at INFO level. It only reports "benchmark completed" with zero metrics.

**Evidence**: Manual execution of guidellm shows:
```
RuntimeError: Backend validation request failed. Could not connect to the server or validate the backend configuration.
```

## Context Gap Check

- [x] Was this caused by missing context? **PARTIAL**

**What was missing**: 
- The guidellm-runner source code is NOT in the ai-aas repository (deployed as pre-built container)
- No documentation that guidellm requires unauthenticated /health endpoint
- No anti-pattern documented for "silent failures in wrapper services"

## Proposed Fix

**Affected components**:
- `services/api-router-service` - Add unauthenticated /health endpoint
- OR guidellm-runner configuration - Skip validation or pass API key in validation
- guidellm-runner wrapper code - Log validation failures at ERROR level

**Fix options** (in priority order):

1. **Option A**: Add unauthenticated health endpoint at `/v1/chat/completions/health`
   - Pros: Standard pattern, guidellm expects this
   - Cons: May expose service status publicly

2. **Option B**: Configure guidellm to skip validation
   - Pros: Quick fix
   - Cons: May miss actual backend issues

3. **Option C**: Fix guidellm-runner wrapper to pass API key during validation
   - Pros: Proper auth, keeps security
   - Cons: Requires access to guidellm-runner source code (not in repo)

**Estimated complexity**: Medium (Option A), Low (Option B)

## Prevention

How to prevent this class of bug in future:

| Type | Action |
|------|--------|
| Logging | guidellm-runner should log validation errors at ERROR level |
| Testing | Add integration test that verifies benchmarks actually send requests |
| Monitoring | Alert if `guidellm_requests_total` stays at 0 for >1 hour |
| Documentation | Document guidellm backend requirements (health endpoints) |

## Follow-up Beads Created

Creating follow-up beads now...

**From Investigation**: ai-aas-fkm6

## Steps to Fix

### 1. Create ghcr-pull-secret in staging cluster

```bash
export KUBECONFIG=~/kubeconfigs/kubeconfig-staging.yaml

  --docker-server=ghcr.io \
